title: 10-day ops onramp cookbook
body:
Purpose:
Brief operational cookbook to move a small pilot from internal beta to a ten-day production onramp while keeping latency, cost, and user-facing error rates within guardrails. Designed to be a tightly scoped, checklist-first artifact for product-ops + SRE + oncall engineers.

Context and constraints:
- Pilot expected: 2k daily active requests (ramp to 20k/day within 10 days depending on uptake).
- Primary SLOs: p95 latency < 450ms for short queries, error rate < 0.5% (inference failures), cost per 1k tokens below target budget lane.
- Model variants available: small-latency (prod-light), balanced (prod-default), high-quality (prod-qual). Routing policy can shift to cheaper variant on sustained cost threshold.
- This doc focuses on the first 10 operational days after opening pilot to invited customers.

Ten-day checklist (day-by-day):
Day 0 (pre-sunrise):
- Confirm capacity commit + autoscale upper bounds with platform-engineering (owner: Liam).
- Create dedicated rollout channel in Slack + incident bridge template.
- Tag telemetry dashboards: route=pilotA, model=prod-default.
- Smoke test traffic generator (10k synthetic tokens across sequences).
Open items: verify KMS rotation window for pilot keys.

Day 1 (open to cohort 1):
- Open canary at 2% traffic with gradual increment script enabled.
- Monitor p50/p95 latencies and token-based cost per-minute.
- QA: sample 25 responses for hallucination regression checks (owner: Priya).
- Ops: ensure fallback policy to prod-light is active at cost_spike > 1.4x baseline.

Day 2-3 (scale to cohort 10):
- Ramp to 10% traffic if latency SLOs hold and error rate < 0.3%.
- Run A/B: 50/50 routing for two prompt templates affecting token counts; capture per-prompt token delta.
- Run quick stress test: 2k concurrent steady-state requests for 5 minutes.

Day 4-5 (mid-ramp):
- Confirm KV cache hit ratio > 18% on conversational flows (owner: Jordan).
- Apply batching window suggestion from Optimize (batch target 40ms) and observe throughput change.
- Update cost forecast sheet (linked) and notify finance if projected 20% budget overspend.

Day 6-7 (validation):
- Validate rollout telemetry for region replication; verify fallback region in case of zone outage.
- Run evaluation checklist: quality regression alerts (example prompts) must be green.
- On-call runbook dry-run: simulate node OOM and validate automatic fallback.

Day 8-9 (scale to broad pilot):
- Ramp to 50-70% of expected steady state (target 10k-14k DAU).
- Turn on sampling for post-generation safety reviews (1% sample).
- Sanity-check billing pipeline: reconcile token counts vs logs.

Day 10 (stability checkpoint):
- Full readiness review: product-ops, infra, SRE, and bizops signoff.
- Decide: widen to open beta / hold / rollback. Document decision in confluence and close this runbook.

KPI snapshot (what we watch every 4 hours for first 72h, then twice daily):
- Traffic: requests/sec (owner: product-ops), trend + growth rate.
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 by route/model (owner: SRE).
- Error rate: inference errors, timeouts, 5xx (owner: SRE).
- Cost: cost per 1k tokens, projection vs budget (owner: finance liaison).
- Quality: prompt-level BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxy and manual sample pass rate (owner: applied-ml).
- Cache hit ratio and batch utilization (owner: infra).
- Fallback activations count and reason codes (owner: platform).
Thresholds and automatic actions (examples):
- If p95 > 550ms for 10 minutes -> throttle nonessential background routes and pause new signups.
- If error rate > 1% for 5 minutes -> automatically shift 30% traffic to prod-light and notify oncall.
- If projected daily cost > budget*1.25 -> trigger manual approval; if unchanged after 30m, shift to prod-light.

Surge and rollback playbook (quick):
- Surge detection: increase > 3x baseline within 10 minutes OR sustained 2x for 30 minutes.
- Immediate actions: enable emergency auto-throttle, scale up reserved pool (if available), enable pre-warmed workers.
- If scaling cannot bring p95 under threshold in 15 minutes -> execute rollback: reduce model to prod-light, disable non-critical pipelines, communicate status.
- Postmortem: timeline + correlated logs + model sample debug.

Notable runbook snippets:
- Canary ramp script (ops): increments at 5m intervals, requires green telemetry for last 15m to proceed.
- Emergency contact list: oncall-sre@redwood, product-ops@redwood, infra-pager.
- Quick rollback command: rhubarb rollback --target prod-light --reason "latency-surge" (placeholder; confirm CLI name).

Telemetry and dashboards to create/update:
- PID dashboard: single pane with p95 latency, error rate, request/s, cost/min, cache_hit%.
- Per-prompt token delta table: shows top 10 prompts with rising token consumption.
- Quality sampling board: stream of 1% sampled responses tagged by prompt and QA pass/fail.

Experimentation plan (live tuning knobs):
- Batching window: test 20ms / 40ms / 80ms for throughput vs latency tradeoff.
- Prefix cache TTL: 10s / 60s / 300s to measure hit rate vs freshness.
- Routing policy: cost-first vs latency-first. Run 24-hour back-to-back experiments and compare cost per useful token.

Stakeholder communication cadence:
- Day 0-3: hourly internal dashboard + once-per-day customer-facing short note (if cohort > 5).
- Day 4-9: 2x daily internal digest, daily external summary to participating customers.
- Day 10: decision memo and next-phase plan.

Open questions (for review):
- What is final acceptance threshold for quality regression (product to define numeric pass rate).
- Confirm CLI names/ops scripts and whether rhubarb exists; otherwise reference the new deploy tool.
- Do we want an automated color-coded email to customers when fallback activates? (privacy + UX question)

Appendix: quick templates and links
- Customer-facing notification template:
  "We observed elevated inference latency on your integration. We temporarily shifted to a lower-latency model variant to preserve availability. We're investigating and will follow up in 2 hours with remediation steps and a timeline."
- Postmortem fields: timeline, impact, root cause, remediation, responsible, follow-ups.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally checklist-first and conservative on automations. If we want more aggressive auto-scaling/auto-shift we should list explicit safety checks and expose an opt-in flag per-customer.
- Please flag any missing owners (I assigned where obvious).
- If you rely on external scripts referenced above, add exact repo/PR links in the linked_artifacts section before signoff.

Last edits: quick tidy by Maya on 2026-03-10.
